question: In Cloudflare's Q3 2024 earnings-call answer about R2 and D1, how did Matthew Prince distinguish their roles in AI workloads, and how did he say these components help customers build applications on Workers? Cite that answer.

answer.answer: In the Q3 2024 call (7-Nov-2024), responding to Jonathan Ho's question on R2 and D1, Matthew Prince framed R2 as the AI-relevant piece: its value is letting customers move large datasets to wherever there is excess GPU capacity, and in training workloads R2 often serves as the gateway into the rest of Cloudflare, which helps win AI workloads, especially inference. D1 he described as less of a direct AI driver — more a traditional SQL database. Together, though, he said the components let customers build full applications on Cloudflare Workers: you need a database and an object store, and these primitives combined let Cloudflare win more complicated applications and workloads. He added that Hyperdrive and the Birthday Week Durable Objects/Durable Databases announcements are unique primitives enabling applications that would previously have been prohibitively difficult to build, especially around worldwide synchronization.

content.text: {"answerable":true,"answer":"In the Q3 2024 call (7-Nov-2024), responding to Jonathan Ho's question on R2 and D1, Matthew Prince framed R2 as the AI-relevant piece: its value is letting customers move large datasets to wherever there is excess GPU capacity, and in training workloads R2 often serves as the gateway into the rest of Cloudflare, which helps win AI workloads, especially inference. D1 he described as less of a direct AI driver — more a traditional SQL database. Together, though, he said the components let customers build full applications on Cloudflare Workers: you need a database and an object store, and these primitives combined let Cloudflare win more complicated applications and workloads.
